title: Carya illinoinensis (Juglandaceae): A new genus and species for the flora of Pakistan
content:
The family Juglandaceae in Pakistan has traditionally been considered monogenic and monospecific, represented only by Juglans regia L. This study provides the first molecular evidence for the presence of C. illinoinensis (Wangenh.) K. Koch (pecan) in the country. Leaf samples collected from northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were analysed using DNA barcoding with nuclear (ITS2) and chloroplast (mat K and rbc L) markers. PCR amplification and sequencing were highly successful (>90%) and BLAST searches revealed greater than 99% similarity with C. illinoinensis accessions from China and the United States. Phylogenetic analysis based on ITS2, mat K and rbc L consistently places the query sample within the Carya clade, clearly separated from Juglans and other genera of Juglandaceae. Strong bootstrap support across datasets confirmed the identity of the specimens as C. illinoinensis. This molecular confirmation extends the known distribution of Carya into South Asia and highlights the utility of DNA barcoding in resolving cryptic taxa and uncovering overlooked species. The discovery adds a new genus and species record to the flora of Pakistan and provides a foundation for further phylogenetic and ecological studies in the region.


Abstract

Carya illinoinensis is recorded in Pakistan (northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) for the first time based on both morphological and molecular data. The discovery also represents the first one at genus rank. Leaf samples were analysed using nuclear (ITS2) and chloroplast (matK and rbcL) markers and compared with database accession especially from China and the United States. Strong bootstrap support across datasets confirmed the identity of the Pakistani specimens as C. illinoinensis. The results confirm that the distribution of Carya into South Asia extends and highlight the utility of DNA barcoding in resolving the identification of difficult taxa and uncovering overlooked species.
